import csv, sys, os, re
input_path = os.path.expanduser('~/Desktop/seguro_wf_eval/h12/customers_raw.csv')
output_path = os.path.expanduser('~/Desktop/seguro_wf_eval/h12/customers_clean.csv')
rows = []
with open(input_path, newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    for row in reader:
        # Trim spaces in name and city
        name = row['name'].strip()
        city = row['city'].strip()
        # Title case city
        city = city.title()
        # Skip rows with missing city after strip
        if city == '':
            continue
        rows.append({'name': name, 'city': city, 'orders': row['orders'].strip()})
# Remove exact duplicate rows
unique = []
seen = set()
for r in rows:
    key = (r['name'], r['city'], r['orders'])
    if key not in seen:
        seen.add(key)
        unique.append(r)
# Write output CSV
with open(output_path, 'w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=['name','city','orders'])
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(unique)
print('DONE', output_path)

Edited by: Priyanka Negi Education Oct 15, 2026 20:30 IST Published On Oct 15, 2026 20:29 IST Last Updated On Oct 15, 2026 20:30 IST Read Time: 2 mins Share Twitter WhatsApp Facebook Reddit Email Eligibility requires graduation with 50 percent marks. Show Quick Read Summary is AI-generated, newsroom-reviewed IIT Delhi has opened applications for the Executive Programme in Robotics starting January 2027 The five-month online course includes classes on Saturdays and alternate Sundays from 10 am to 2:30 pm Graduates with at least 50% marks are eligible to apply for the robotics programme What career roles can graduates apply for after completion? The Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT Delhi) has opened applications for the fourth batch of its Executive Programme in Robotics. The five-month online programme is offered through the institute's Continuing Education Programme (CEP). The course is designed to help learners understand robotics, robot control and the use of artificial intelligence in robotic systems. According to the official programme page, classes will begin on January 30, 2027, and continue until June 26, 2027. The Continuing Education Programme (CEP), #IITDelhi, has launched "Executive Programme in Robotics (Batch 04)". Details: https://t.co/9TQb1kto5X Apply Now Link: https://t.co/NmXLIZ2yRU Last Date to Apply: 29th January 2027 https://t.co/1BqOlHNVKh — IIT Delhi (@iitdelhi) October 15, 2026 IIT Delhi Robotics Programme: Who Can Apply? Candidates who have completed graduation with at least 50% marks are eligible to apply for the programme. The course is offered online, with classes scheduled for Saturdays and alternate Sundays from 10 am to 2:30 pm. What Will Students Learn? The programme covers the basics of robotics and automation, along with the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning in robotic systems. Participants will learn about robot design, sensors, motion control and the technologies used to build and operate robots. The curriculum also includes robot simulation, embedded systems and the use of programming tools. The course follows a practical approach, with 40% of the learning focused on theory and 60% on practical work. Participants will also get an opportunity to build a functional robot as part of the programme. IIT Delhi Robotics Course: Fees And Last Date To Apply The programme fee is Rs 1,69,000, plus 18% Goods and Services Tax (GST). Candidates must also pay a non-refundable application fee of Rs 1,000. According to the official programme page, the application deadline is October 17, 2026. Interested candidates can submit their applications through the official website. Got a follow‑up question on this article? Go on Does IIT Delhi offer placement assistance for this robotics programme? How will students build physical robots during an online course? What programming languages do participants need to know beforehand? import os
import glob
import pandas as pd

folder_path = 'C:\Users\omsal\Desktop\seguro_wf_eval\w7'
file_paths = glob.glob(os.path.join(folder_path, '*.txt'))

word_counts = []
for file_path in file_paths:
    with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as file:
        text = file.read()
        words = text.split()
        word_count = len(words)
        word_counts.append({'file': os.path.basename(file_path), 'word_count': word_count})

# Save to Excel
output_file = os.path.join(folder_path, 'word_counts.xlsx')

# Create DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame(word_counts)

# Save to Excel with a bar chart
with pd.ExcelWriter(output_file, engine='openpyxl') as writer:
    df.to_excel(writer, index=False, sheet_name='Word Counts')
    chart = writer.book.create_chart({'type': 'bar'})
    chart.add_series({'source': 'Word Counts!$A$2:$B$' + str(len(df) + 1)})
    chart.set_title({'name': 'Word Counts'})
    chart.set_x_axis({'name': 'File'})
    chart.set_y_axis({'name': 'Word Count'})
    chart.set_position({'x': 2, 'y': 0})
    writer.sheets['Word Counts'].insert_chart('B2', chart)

print(f'Word counts saved to {output_file}')

"""textstats module
Provides utilities for simple text analysis.
"""
import re
from collections import Counter

def word_frequencies(text: str) -> dict:
    """Return a dictionary mapping each lowercase word to its count.

    Punctuation is ignored and words are split on any non‑alphabetic characters.
    The function normalises all words to lowercase.
    """
    # Use regex to find words consisting of alphabetic characters (including apostrophes inside words)
    words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z]+", text.lower())
    return dict(Counter(words))
